⬢ Character Sheet · 5e

⬢ Universal Character Sheet

D&D 5e · offline · one file

This is your whole character sheet in a single file. No Adobe, no login, no hosted app. It works offline in any browser, and it autosaves in this one, though it's worth pressing Save now and then for a backup.

Print it blank for the table, or let it build your character and auto-calculate everything as you play. You can keep several characters in here and switch between them from Manage Characters up top. Upload a portrait and it even makes a printable paper mini.

Fill it in with Create Character. This sheet is built to be filled out by the Create Character process, not typed in by hand. It walks you through race, class, background, and feats, then keeps everything (modifiers, AC, saves, spell DC, attacks, HP, and more) calculated and correct as you go. Unless you really know the rules, start there.

Manual overrides (advanced). You can still pin any calculated value by hand: double-click it on a computer, or long-press it on a phone or tablet. It's meant for homebrew, table rulings, and the odd item the rules engine doesn't know about. A pinned value stops auto-updating, so use it sparingly. To undo one, Alt-click it (or long-press and clear it), or clear them all under Settings → Manual overrides.

Click "Create Character" to get started!

Characters

Each character is its own siloed sheet — separate sources, rules, pages, and portrait.

Import characters

Each ticked character is added as a new card here. Nothing already in this browser is replaced, so importing another copy of a character you already have just gives you a second version of it.

Export sourcebooks

Each ticked book is written as its own source-data.json, bundled together in a single .zip. Re-import any of them later with Import files…

Ability Score Improvements & Feats

Your class grants an Ability Score Improvement at certain levels — for each, take either an ASI (+2 to one ability, or +1 to two) or a Feat. Some races (Variant Human, Custom Lineage) also grant a feat.

Choose Your Tools

A proficiency you were granted lets you pick the specific kind. Choose one for each below.

Settings

Fetches the newest version of the whole app from the web and reloads. Your loaded character and sourcebooks are kept (they live in your browser, not in the file). Save a copy first (the Save button in the toolbar) in case a new version misbehaves.

A dark colour theme for low-light play. This applies across all of your characters. Printing always uses the light theme.

Turns off all motion (like the shimmer on the level-up button) for a calmer, distraction-free sheet during play. This applies across all of your characters.

Reopens the short intro that appears the first time you open this sheet.

Double-click any calculated value on the sheet (ability scores, modifiers, proficiency, AC, initiative, saves, skills, spell DC, attacks, HP…) to pin a custom value. A pinned source value still feeds everything below it. Pinned fields are outlined with a small marker and their tooltip shows the calculated value; Alt-click one to revert. On a phone or tablet, long-press a field to edit it, and clear the value to revert it to calculated. This button clears them all at once.

Downloads a fresh copy with no characters and default settings, but with every sourcebook you've loaded baked in. Good for handing someone a ready-to-use sheet. It opens blank for them (and for you), and it keeps your own characters and settings untouched.

⚠ Work in progress. The Universal Character Sheet (default) is a landscape dashboard on screen that prints as the classic portrait sheet. Classic is a pixel rebuild of the official 5e sheet. Both are still being refined — expect the occasional rough edge or change between versions.

The look of this character's sheet — its colours, borders, and surfaces. Each character can have its own theme. Dark mode (Settings → General → Appearance) layers on top of any theme and stays one setting across all your characters. Printing always uses the light look.

Unchecked pages are removed from the tab bar and won't print. (The Mini page also needs a portrait.)

Removes the portrait box on the Core page from both the tab view and print. Your uploaded image is kept.

Off by default. When on, the Carrying Capacity card adds the Encumbered (×5) and Heavily Encumbered (×10) thresholds and applies their speed penalties. When off, only your Max Carry (×15) and Push/Drag/Lift (×30) are shown.

Off by default. When off, modern gear (pistols, rifles, shotguns, dynamite, etc.) is hidden from the item search and the per-row item autocomplete.

Off by default. When off, futuristic gear (laser/antimatter weapons, powered armor, etc.) is hidden from the item search and the per-row item autocomplete.

Every optional rule is on by default. The origin rules change what the creation wizard lets you customize; the class-feature rules add the feature to a character that has the class (limited-use ones get a tracker, and a few replace a base feature). Changes apply when you next create or edit a character.

The button (on every Spells page) creates extra, independent spell sheets — handy for another class's spell list. Turning this off only hides the button; any spell sheets you've already created stay exactly as they are.

49 books loaded — 505 spells, 16 classes, 126 races.

Loads any book straight from your local 5etools server (works offline; keep that server running). Loaded books are remembered in this browser. Reload all loaded sources re-fetches them to refresh their data.

Import files… adds one or more source-data.json files as extra sourcebooks, merged into whatever's already loaded (it never replaces what you have — same as loading a book from the server). Export books as JSON… does the reverse: pick which loaded books to write out and it splits each into its own source-data.json, bundled in a .zip, so you can back them up or share a single book (each re-imports as one book). In the loaded-sources list above, the ✕ next to a book deletes it from this browser entirely (with confirmation). A browser can't overwrite the open file, so loaded books live in this browser until you bake them into a file. Save (top bar) bakes them in alongside your character; Export a blank sheet (Settings → General) bakes them into a blank copy with no character. Keep either to make the books permanent. Clear loaded books forgets everything loaded in this browser and reverts to the data baked into this file.
